notes: The DMI response is a record port and its data field is treated as a carrier or observation path rather than a primary asset.
C3's Phase 1 held-line list includes line 654, which is the reset assignment to dci.data_reg rather than a normal data-production assignment.
The RTL has no port-to-port path for any listed conceptual asset with no intervening point.

points.reason: This generate branch ties authentication validity to a constant and provides no runtime path to modify or block the validity state.
The black-box authenticator receives write, read, data, enable, clock and reset inputs and produces auth.valid, so the stated black-box rule permits corruption or suppression of validity.
auth.valid gates the DMI read enable, so an altered validity value can admit an unauthenticated read or block an authenticated read.
auth.valid gates the DMI write enable, so an altered validity value can admit an unauthenticated write or block an authenticated write.
auth.valid gates halt_req_o, allowing invalid authentication to assert or suppress hart-control behavior.
auth.valid gates the debug-module reset output, so validity corruption can change or block reset control.
auth.valid conditionally permits DMI status, control, data and authentication reads, so corruption can expose unauthorized behavior or suppress authorized responses.
An authenticated DMI write at the dmcontrol address stores a new hartsel value, which can redirect or disable subsequent hart operations.
The decoder converts hartsel into the one-hot hartsel_dec target, so a corrupted decode can select the wrong hart or no valid hart.
The decoded selection determines which halt request vector bit is asserted, allowing control to reach an unintended hart or none.
hartsel_dec qualifies command validation, execution requests and completion checks, so corruption can redirect or prevent the selected-hart command.
hartsel_dec chooses which hart receives resume and reset-status updates, allowing status and control state to be applied to the wrong hart.
The decoded selection chooses which hart's reset, resume and halt status is returned, so corruption can report or operationally target the wrong hart.
bus_access stores DMI or bus data in dci.data_reg and returns that register through the bus response, allowing overwriting or observation of hart debug data.
An authenticated DMI data-register read copies dci.data_reg into dmi_rsp_o.data, exposing the retained hart debug word.
rden controls whether the bus response returns dci.data_reg, making it a release-control point for the data.
dci.data_reg_we selects the DMI data write into dci.data_reg, so manipulating it can overwrite a retained hart debug word.
An authenticated dmcontrol write stores halt_req, allowing the DMI path to assert or suppress the halt command.
The decoded hart selection determines which halt_req_o vector bit receives the command.
The request generator combines halt_req with hart selection, module activation and authentication before driving the hart-control output.
Under the black-box rule, the authenticator's validity output can be corrupted or withheld and line 500 uses it to gate the halt request.
The reset output is not on the halt-request path and does not store, carry or control halt_req_o.
busy is derived from the controller state and directly determines whether the command engine is idle or active.

The controller enters and leaves busy operation through state transitions driven by execution and halt acknowledgements, so altered transitions can create unsafe overlap or a permanent busy condition.
Bus writes generate the acknowledgement inputs that advance or complete the controller, so manipulating them can falsely complete or stall the busy state.
The hart-halted status is used during command checking and can affect whether the controller proceeds or enters an error state.
busy blocks command, autoexec and program-buffer writes and records access errors while active, but this block does not modify busy itself.
busy reports active operation and causes prohibited reads to set rd_acc_err, but the read process does not change the busy state.
busy suppresses DMI data-register writes during an active command, so this point can block later debug operation but cannot modify busy.
